title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option 33: The USA, 1954–75: conflict at home and abroad

exam_structure.overview: Section A tests source inference (4m) and causation (12m). Section B tests historical interpretations and contemporary source utility (36m) plus 4 marks for SPaG.

sections.title: Key topic 1: The development of the civil rights movement, 1954–60

topics.title: 1. The position of Black Americans in the early 1950s
points: Segregation, discrimination & voting rights in the Southern states
Work of civil rights organisations (incl. the NAACP & CORE)

topics.title: 2. Developments in education
points: Causes, features & impact: Brown v. Topeka case (1954)
Causes, features & impact: events at Little Rock High School (1957)

topics.title: 3. The Montgomery Bus Boycott and its impact, 1955–60
points: Causes & events of the Montgomery Bus Boycott; Rosa Parks
Success & impact of boycott; The Supreme Court ruling; The Civil Rights Act (1957)
Leadership & impact of Martin Luther King; founding the SCLC

topics.title: 4. Opposition to the civil rights movement
points: The Ku Klux Klan & violence (incl. the murder of Emmet Till in 1955)
Opposition to desegregation in the South (incl. the ‘Dixiecrats’ & founding White Citizens’ Councils)

sections.title: Key topic 2: Protest, progress and radicalism, 1960–75

topics.title: 1. Developments, 1960–62
points: Significance: Greensboro & the sit-in movement
Causes, features & impact: Freedom Riders (incl. Ku Klux Klan violence & the Anniston bomb (1961)
The James Meredith case (1962)

topics.title: 2. Peaceful protests and their impact, 1963–65
points: King & the peace marches of 1963 in Birmingham & Washington
Freedom Summer & the Mississippi murders
Impact of peaceful protest & the roles of Presidents Kennedy & Johnson passing the Civil Rights Act (1964); Selma & the Voting Rights Act (1965)

topics.title: 3. Malcolm X and Black Power, 1963–70
points: Malcolm X, his beliefs, methods & involvement with the Black Muslims; His later change of attitude & assassination
Emergence of Black Power; Stokely Carmichael & the 1968 Mexico Olympics
Methods & achievements of the Black Panther movement

topics.title: 4. The civil rights movement, 1965–75
points: Riots of 1965–67 & the Kerner Report (1968)
King’s campaign in the North; assassination of Martin Luther King & its impact
Scale of progress in civil rights by 1975

sections.title: Key topic 3: US involvement in the Vietnam War, 1954–75

topics.title: 1. Reasons for US involvement in the conflict in Vietnam, 1954–63
points: Expanded US involvement under Eisenhower (incl. the domino theory & weaknesses of the Diem government)
Greater involvement under Kennedy (incl. the overthrow of Diem & the Strategic Hamlet Program)

topics.title: 2. Escalation of the conflict under Johnson
points: Escalation of conflict & increased US involvement in Vietnam (incl. the increasing threat of the Vietcong & the Gulf of Tonkin incident (1964)

topics.title: 3. The nature of the conflict in Vietnam, 1964–68
points: Guerrilla tactics used by the Vietcong
Methods used by the USA (incl. Search & Destroy, Operation Rolling Thunder & chemical weapons)
Features & impact: Tet Offensive, 1968

topics.title: 4. Changes under Nixon, 1969–73
points: Key features: Vietnamisation; Causes of its failure
The Nixon Doctrine & the withdrawal of US troops
Attacks on Cambodia (1970) & Laos (1971) & the bombing of North Vietnam (1972)

sections.title: Key topic 4: Reactions to, and the end of, US involvement in

topics.title: 1. Opposition to the war
points: Growth of opposition (incl. the student movement, TV & media coverage of the war & the draft system)
Public reaction to the My Lai Massacre (1968); trial of Lt. Calley
The Kent State University shootings (1970)

topics.title: 2. Support for the war
points: Causes of support for the war (incl. the fear of communism)
The ‘hard hats’ & the ‘silent majority’

topics.title: 3. The peace process and end of the war
points: Causes & key features: peace negotiations (1972–73)
Significance: Paris Peace Agreement (1973)
Economic & human costs of the war for the USA

topics.title: 4. Reasons for the failure of the USA in Vietnam
points: Strengths of North Vietnam (incl. Russian & Chinese support, Vietcong tactics & the Ho Chi Minh Trail)
Weaknesses of the US armed forces; failure of US tactics
Impact of opposition to the war in the USA
